newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to expand privatisation, minister says.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to expand privatisation, minister says.

text.p: Morocco is looking at expanding its privatisation programme after four years of selling off companies and hotels at an average rate of one a month, Privatisation Minister Abderrahman Saaidi said on Friday.
Saaidi, addressing a capital markets and investment forum, said that from the present list of 77 companies and 36 hotels, a total of 49 firms and hotels had been sold.
This had raised more than 10 billion dirhams ($1.1 billion) with buyers pledged to invest about 2.2 billion dirhams more.
"A sub-cabinet commission is now examining a proposal to greatly expand the list of privatisables," he said.
He added: "We are certain that the state should get out of direct production and let the private sector do its job."
In the next few months, within the existing programme, SMI, (Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter) a diversified mining holding, would be listed on the stock exchange, and other sales were being completed.
The ministry would soon be tendering three sugar refineries and would later sell seven other sugar mills, he said.
Parliament was still looking at proposed privatisation of telecommunications, and Morocco planned to issue a licence for a second mobile phone system provider.

Saaidi said that for big public enterprises, Morocco wanted to convert large government authorities to corporations which would be a first step to prepare firms for listing part of their shares on the exchange.
Concessions for water and electricity distribution were being negotiated for Casablanca and a similar accord could be seen for Rabat.
"In the long run, we expect to see the private sector providing most public utilities and much infrastructure," he said.
